audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 11, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, reception-history, and political audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for foreign-wife blame, plural marriage and concubinage, interfaith worship, gendered responsibility, Edomite massacre, child refugee Hadad, Egyptian asylum, adversary theology, forced labor, prophetic succession, attempted political killing, and imperial collapse.

verses.restored: King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides Pharaoh's daughter: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women.

From nations of which YHWH said to children of Israel, You shall not enter among them and they shall not enter among you, for surely they will turn your heart after their gods. Solomon clung to them in love.
He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; his wives turned his heart.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with YHWH his Divine as heart of David his father.
Solomon walked after Ashtoreth goddess of Sidonians and after Milcom detestable thing/god of Ammonites.
Solomon did evil in eyes of YHWH and did not fully follow YHWH as David his father.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, detestable thing/god of Moab, on hill before Jerusalem, and for Molech, detestable thing/god of children of Ammon.
Thus he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
YHWH became angry with Solomon because his heart turned from YHWH, Divine of Israel, who appeared to him twice,
and commanded him concerning this matter not to walk after other gods; but he did not keep what YHWH commanded.
YHWH said to Solomon, Because this is with you and you did not keep my covenant and statutes I commanded, tearing I will tear kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
Yet in your days I will not do it, for sake of David your father; from hand of your son I will tear it.
Only I will not tear away all kingdom; one tribe I will give to your son for sake of David my servant and Jerusalem which I chose.
YHWH raised an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, from royal seed in Edom.
When David was in Edom and Joab commander of army went up to bury slain, after striking every male in Edom—
for six months Joab remained there with all Israel until he cut off every male in Edom—
Hadad fled, he and Edomite men from servants of his father with him, to go to Egypt; Hadad was a small child.
They arose from Midian, came to Paran, took men from Paran with them, and came to Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave him a house, appointed food for him, and gave him land.
Hadad found great favor in eyes of Pharaoh, who gave him as wife sister of his own wife, sister of Tahpenes the queen.
Sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house; Genubath was in Pharaoh's household among Pharaoh's sons.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David lay with his ancestors and Joab commander of army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Send me away, that I may go to my land.
Pharaoh said, What have you lacked with me that you seek to go to your land? He said, Nothing, but sending, send me away.
Divine raised another adversary against Solomon: Rezon son of Eliada, who fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men to himself and became commander of a band when David killed those of Zobah. They went to Damascus, lived there, and reigned in Damascus.
He was an adversary to Israel all days of Solomon, besides evil Hadad did. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, Solomon's servant, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow woman—he lifted his hand against king.
This was matter for which he lifted hand against king: Solomon built Millo and closed breach of City of David his father.
The man Jeroboam was a mighty man of ability. Solomon saw young man was doing work and appointed him over all forced labor of house of Joseph.
At that time Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and Ahijah the Shilonite prophet found him on road. Ahijah had covered himself with a new garment, and the two were alone in field.
Ahijah grasped new garment upon him and tore it into twelve pieces.
He said to Jeroboam, Take ten pieces, for thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: Look, I am tearing kingdom from hand of Solomon and giving you ten tribes.
But one tribe shall be his for sake of David my servant and Jerusalem, city I chose from all tribes of Israel.

Because they abandoned me, bowed to Ashtoreth goddess of Sidonians, Chemosh god of Moab, and Milcom god of children of Ammon, and did not walk in my ways to do upright in my eyes and keep my statutes and judgments as David his father.
But I will not take all kingdom from his hand. I will make him leader all days of his life for sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commands and statutes.
I will take kingdom from hand of his son and give you ten tribes.
To his son I will give one tribe, so David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, city I chose to put my name there.
I will take you, and you shall reign according to all your soul desires and be king over Israel.

If you listen to all I command, walk in my ways, do upright in my eyes, and keep my statutes and commands as David my servant did, I will be with you, build you an enduring house as I built for David, and give Israel to you.
I will afflict seed of David because of this, but not all days.
Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam. Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until Solomon's death.
Rest of acts of Solomon, all he did, and his wisdom—are they not written in book of acts of Solomon?
Days Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.
Solomon lay with his ancestors and was buried in City of David his father. Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

translation_notes: The chapter blames foreign wives for turning Solomon's heart, but Solomon is the king who accumulated one thousand women within a system of dynastic marriage, concubinage, and likely coercion. Responsibility belongs to him, not to women's ethnicity.

Foreign women and their religions must not be portrayed as inherently corrupting. Interfaith contact is not the same as imperial accumulation, coercive marriage, or abandoning covenantal responsibility.
The labels 'detestable thing' reflect polemical religious language. They may not justify persecution, vandalism, forced conversion, antisemitism, Islamophobia, or contempt toward living traditions.
Hadad's story reveals the imperial violence hidden beneath Solomon's peace: David and Joab killed every male in Edom over six months, and a small child fled into Egyptian asylum.
Hadad's desire to return home is not irrational ingratitude toward Egypt; refugees may value safety and still long for homeland.
Rezon's movement also emerges from Davidic war. Political adversaries are survivors and agents, not merely instruments raised to punish Solomon.
Jeroboam is first a supervisor inside Solomon's forced-labor system. The coming rupture is tied to exploitation as well as prophetic symbolism.
The narrative praises David's obedience in sweeping terms despite the books' own record. Royal idealization must be held beside Bathsheba, Uriah, census plague, Edom, and other harms.
Solomon attempts to kill a political rival, driving Jeroboam into the same Egyptian asylum that sheltered Hadad.
safety_note: Do not blame women, foreigners, interfaith relationships, aging, or minority religions for Solomon's collapse. Center royal accumulation, coercive marriage, forced labor, imperial massacre, refugee survival, and attempted political assassination.
